source_refs.note: 2- Building a primer: a main subheading of 19.3.3 Mechanism of DNA Replication, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 126-127.

blocks.text: On the exposed strands, new DNA cannot be formed unless some nucleotides are already arranged on template. For this purpose, an enzyme primase attaches some RNA nucleotides in front of each template strand at replication origin site. This short fragment of 5-10 RNA nucleotides is called primer.

blocks.alt: A replication bubble: the double helix opens in the middle and a replication fork lies at each end. At each fork gyrase sits on the duplex ahead and helicase at the fork; yellow single-strand binding proteins hold the separated strands apart; a purple primase lays a short primer on a template strand near each fork. The duplex ends are marked 5' and 3'.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.10: Replication - opening up of strands and primer attachment (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.10).
